dossier.purpose: Python SDK (openhands-sdk, -tools, -workspace, -agent-server, all 1.50.1) plus a FastAPI Agent Server and a TypeScript client for building and running coding agents. Two agent kinds: a native LiteLLM-driven tool-calling loop (terminal, file editor, browser, sub-agents, MCP client), and an ACP-delegated agent that spawns Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI / Kimi / Pi / OpenCode adapters. Conversations are event-sourced to disk. They run on the host by default, or inside Docker, Apptainer, Kubernetes agent-sandbox, or hosted OpenHands runtimes. It is an agent framework and runtime, not a scheduler (scheduling lives in the separate OpenHands/automation repo) and not a dedicated research harness.

claims.claim: The SDK 'provides Python, TypeScript, and REST APIs for building agents that work with code'.
Named use cases: one-off tasks (e.g. a README for your repo), routine maintenance (e.g. updating dependencies), and major multi-agent tasks (refactors, rewrites).
Agents can use the local machine as their workspace, or run inside ephemeral workspaces (e.g. in Docker or Kubernetes) using the Agent Server.
The SDK is 'the engine behind the OpenHands CLI and OpenHands Cloud'.
Quick Start: LLM(model='gpt-5.5', api_key=LLM_API_KEY) + Agent(TerminalTool, FileEditorTool, TaskTrackerTool) + Conversation(agent, workspace=cwd), then send_message(...) and run().
Installation is in the external Getting Started Guide (docs.openhands.dev/sdk/getting-started); for local development run `make build` (workspace dependencies + pre-commit hooks).

This repo owns the Python SDK, Agent Server, REST/WebSocket API and the browser-compatible TypeScript client. OpenHands/automation owns scheduling, webhooks, run history and dispatch. 'The SDK/Agent Server executes the conversations dispatched by automation.'
Docs at docs.openhands.dev/sdk cover architecture, guides (custom tools, MCP, skills) and an Agent Server REST API reference.
With AgentContext(load_public_skills=True) the default OpenHands/extensions marketplace supplies skills such as uv and deno, picked up from markers like uv.lock or deno.json.
SWE-bench score badge 'SWEBench-77.6' linking to a Google Sheet.
Tech report arXiv 2511.03690 ('The OpenHands Software Agent SDK: A Composable and Extensible Foundation for Production Agents'); license badge says MIT.

(AgentSandboxWorkspace README) Runs the agent server in a Kubernetes pod claimed from a SandboxWarmPool for sub-second starts. Adds native pause/resume, persistent-volume workspace state across suspend, and gVisor/Kata isolation via runtimeClass on the SandboxTemplate.
(agent-server README) Product-analytics telemetry is disabled by default and does nothing unless a deployment opts in; it never sends prompts, messages, file contents, paths, secrets or tracebacks.

install.method: From source with uv (README and DEVELOPMENT.md); make build runs `uv sync --dev` plus `pre-commit install` and requires uv >= 0.8.13
install.command: git clone https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk.git && cd software-agent-sdk && make build

install.method: PyPI packages (openhands-sdk, openhands-tools, openhands-workspace, openhands-agent-server). The README defers to an external Getting Started page that was not opened; command and package names come from an issue-template placeholder and the release workflow
PyPI extra for the Kubernetes agent-sandbox workspace
Agent server from a source checkout (after make build)
Agent-server Docker image on GHCR (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). The tag in the doc is a specific commit tag; the code default is ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:latest-python
pip install from git (used in the example CI workflows)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - unit-test jobs run on Linux runners (.github/workflows/tests.yml:70,146,196,329,428,483); the agent-server binary is built and /health-smoke-tested on ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 (.github/workflows/release-binaries.yml:72-74,111-158); GHCR images are published for linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/server.yml:320-328).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2 documentation or CI. The only mention is an OS option 'WSL on Windows' in the bug template (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_template.yml:133). Native Windows is built and partly tested (tests.yml:253-325; release-binaries.yml:86-88), and the Linux terminal backends (tmux, else subprocess; openhands-tools/openhands/tools/terminal/terminal/factory.py:155-170) would apply, but that is not documented.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes (build + smoke test only) - the agent-server binary is built and /health-smoke-tested on macos-14 arm64 (.github/workflows/release-binaries.yml:83-85,111-158) and server.yml's binary job includes macos-latest (server.yml:37-42). The pytest suites in tests.yml run only on Linux plus a Windows tools subset, none on macOS. DockerWorkspace defaults to platform linux/amd64 (openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace/docker/workspace.py:104-106), so Apple-silicon hosts run the amd64 image under emulation unless platform is overridden. Apptainer is documented only for Linux packages (apptainer/README.md:14-27).
platforms.gpu: yes - optional passthrough only, not required. DockerWorkspace(enable_gpu=True) adds `--gpus all` (openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace/docker/workspace.py:111-114,226-228); ApptainerWorkspace(enable_gpu=True) uses `--nv` (openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace/apptainer/README.md:74-89). Inference is done by external endpoints via LiteLLM (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/llm.py:79-92); an in-cluster Ollama test exists (agent_sandbox/README.md:62-65); no GPU CI.

integrations.cli: No task-running CLI in this repo: README says the OpenHands CLI is a separate repo (README.md:40-41). Only the server entry ships: console script `agent-server` (openhands-agent-server/pyproject.toml:57-58) and `python -m openhands.agent_server` (agent-server README.md:29-44), plus dev utility scripts under scripts/.
integrations.mcp: MCP client only. Agent(mcp_config={...}) consumes MCP servers through FastMCP (examples/01_standalone_sdk/07_mcp_integration.py:41-55; openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/mcp/), and ACPAgent forwards them to the ACP CLI (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py:739-749). POST /api/mcp/test only probes a candidate MCP config (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/mcp_router.py:1-18). No MCP server exposing OpenHands found (no FastMCP server construction outside tests).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK (`from openhands.sdk import LLM, Agent, Conversation, Tool`, README.md:52). REST+WebSocket Agent Server with OpenAPI at /docs (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/api.py:423-493; agent-server README.md:372-378). Stateless OpenAI-compatible /v1 gateway: no stream, store, previous_response_id, and tools are ignored (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/openai/README.md:1-31). TypeScript client @openhands/typescript-client (clients/typescript/package.json:2-4), labelled alpha and remote-only (clients/typescript/README.md:3-15).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: README: none found (README.md does not mention ACP, Claude Code or Codex). Code and examples: ACPAgent (Agent Client Protocol) delegates each turn to a spawned ACP CLI. Built-in providers: claude-code (@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp 0.63.0), codex (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.10.0), gemini-cli, kimi-code, pi, opencode, plus 'custom' (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/settings/acp_providers.py:506-700; settings/acp_install_catalog.py:101-179; agent/acp_agent.py:1-15,1714-1808). Examples: examples/01_standalone_sdk/40_acp_agent_example.py (Claude Code via npx) and examples/02_remote_agent_server/09_acp_agent_with_remote_runtime.py (claude-agent-acp preinstalled in the agent-server image, run in a remote sandbox). A Codex ChatGPT-subscription auth.json can be supplied as reserved secret CODEX_AUTH_JSON (acp_providers.py:451-459). The ACP server owns its own LLM, tools and execution (acp_agent.py:3-8) and permission requests are auto-approved (acp_agent.py:1602-1619). Also: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md are read as third-party skill files (skills/utils.py:343-346), Claude-Code-format plugins and marketplaces are accepted (plugin/format/claude_code.py:1-5; marketplace/types.py:21), and hooks use Claude Code's exit-code contract (hooks/executor.py:34-43). The repo does not name or use the vendors' own SDK packages (no claude-agent-sdk or Codex SDK reference).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Opt-in only, nothing found that phones home by default. (1) Agent-server product telemetry: exporter defaults to 'none'. Delivery needs an exporter (posthog extra plus OH_TELEMETRY_POSTHOG_API_KEY, or an http endpoint) AND granted consent; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 forces it off; only allow-listed lifecycle/failure properties are sent (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/README.md:102-249; agent_server/config.py:133-161; telemetry/policy.py:98-102,160-216; telemetry/service.py:101-146). (2) Laminar/OpenTelemetry tracing: `lmnr` is a hard dependency (openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml:25) but initialises only when LMNR_PROJECT_API_KEY or an OTEL_* endpoint env var is set; default Laminar base URL https://api.lmnr.ai (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/observability/laminar.py:27-32,63-135,244-260). (3) LLM.log_completions defaults False and logs to local disk (llm/llm.py:519-529). (4) No update-check code found; importing the SDK prints a stderr banner, suppressible with OPENHANDS_SUPPRESS_BANNER (sdk/banner.py:15-43). (5) LiteLLM fetches its model-price/capability JSON from its upstream main at import, and the SDK sets no override (tests/sdk/llm/test_model_features.py:3-6; no LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP anywhere in the repo). (6) Accounts and services needed depend on mode: an LLM provider key via LiteLLM (LLM_API_KEY, README.md:60); or the OpenHands proxy for openhands/<model> ids (https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev, llm/utils/openhands_provider.py:11); or ChatGPT-subscription OAuth against auth.openai.com with requests to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (llm/auth/openai.py:122-125,806-811); or an ACP vendor CLI with its own credentials (acp_providers.py:506-560). ACP adapters are fetched from npm with `npx -y --prefer-offline <pinned pkg>` at runtime unless baked into the image (acp_install_catalog.py:78-98; agent_server/docker/Dockerfile:178-236). (7) Optional hosted or third-party services: APIRemoteWorkspace calls the OpenHands runtime API with an API key (openhands-workspace/.../remote_api/workspace.py:19-27,44-45); OpenHandsCloudWorkspace calls app.all-hands.dev with a cloud API key (cloud/workspace.py:53-56,113-125); GraySwanAnalyzer sends conversation history to api.grayswan.ai (openhands-sdk/.../security/grayswan/analyzer.py:28-68); the built-in web-researcher subagent uses Tavily (TAVILY_API_KEY, npx tavily-mcp@0.2.1) and mcp-server-fetch via uvx (openhands-tools/openhands/tools/preset/subagents/web_researcher.md:10-18); public skills are a git clone of github.com/OpenHands/extensions, ref main by default, only if load_public_skills=True, which defaults to False (sdk/context/agent_context.py:101-109; sdk/skills/skill.py:1143-1146,1233-1238); an AUTOMATION_CALLBACK_URL completion POST is sent only if that env var is set (sdk/workspace/base.py:87-117). (8) browser-use (hard dependency of openhands-tools, openhands-tools/pyproject.toml:15, locked 0.11.9) pulls in posthog per the comment at openhands-agent-server/pyproject.toml:24-26. This repo has no setting for browser-use's own telemetry (no ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY match); that library's upstream default was not verified. (9) CI-only: eval workflows dispatch to OpenHands/evaluation (.github/workflows/run-eval.yml:11-13) and example/integration runs use the OpenHands LLM proxy with repo secrets (run-examples.yml:68-80).

code.architecture: Monorepo of four PEP 420 namespace packages under openhands.* plus a TypeScript client. (1) openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/: llm/ (LiteLLM wrapper llm.py; capability registry utils/model_features.py; curated lists utils/verified_models.py; ChatGPT-subscription OAuth auth/openai.py; fallback and router), agent/ (agent.py native tool loop; acp_agent.py ACP delegation; base.py), conversation/ (conversation.py factory -> impl/local_conversation.py or impl/remote_conversation.py; event-sourced state.py persisted as base_state.json + events/event-*.json, persistence_const.py; secret_registry.py), tool/ registry and built-ins (Finish, Think), security/ (confirmation policies; pattern, policy-rail, LLM, GraySwan and ToolShield analyzers), hooks/, mcp/ (client), context/ (prompts, condensers), skills/, plugin/, marketplace/, subagent/, workspace/ (Local/Remote bases), settings/ (AgentSettings; ACP provider registry acp_providers.py and npm pins acp_install_catalog.py), observability/laminar.py. (2) openhands-tools/openhands/tools/: terminal (tmux, subprocess or PowerShell), file_editor, apply_patch, grep, glob, browser_use (browser-use + Playwright/Chromium), task_tracker, task (sub-agent delegation), delegate, planning_file_editor, gemini/*, ask_oracle, tom_consult, workflow; presets in preset/ and built-in sub-agents as markdown in preset/subagents/ (default, code_explorer, bash_runner, web_researcher). (3) openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace/: docker/, apptainer/, agent_sandbox/ (Kubernetes agent-sandbox), remote_api/ (OpenHands runtime API), cloud/ (OpenHands Cloud). (4) openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/: api.py, __main__.py, routers, conversation_service.py + event_service.py (lifecycle, resume, crash recovery), conversation_lease.py (ownership leases), docker_runtime/ (optional per-conversation hardened containers, code-only, no doc found), persistence/ (file-based settings and secrets), telemetry/, openai/ (OpenAI-compatible gateway), docker/Dockerfile + build.py, agent-server.spec (PyInstaller). (5) clients/typescript/: generated OpenAPI types plus handwritten remote-conversation clients. Control flow: Conversation(agent, workspace) with a local path runs the agent loop in-process and tools execute on the host. With a RemoteWorkspace (Docker, Apptainer, Kubernetes, API/Cloud) it becomes a RemoteConversation talking REST/WebSocket to an agent-server inside the sandbox. ACPAgent instead spawns an ACP CLI that owns its own LLM, tools and execution. Defaults: NeverConfirm policy (state.py:123), 500 iterations (conversation.py:132), tool_concurrency_limit 1 (agent/base.py:293-302), LLM default model gpt-5.6 (llm/llm.py:272-276).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: (a) four PyPI packages (openhands-sdk/-tools/-workspace/-agent-server, all 1.50.1) published by `uv publish --token` with the long-lived PYPI_TOKEN_OPENHANDS secret; the workflow has no id-token permission and no attestation step (.github/workflows/pypi-release.yml:20-22,51-87). (b) TypeScript client to npm via OIDC trusted publishing with `--provenance`, and to GitHub Packages (typescript-client-npm-publish.yml:16-18,68; .github/workflows/README-RELEASE.md:47-48). (c) agent-server PyInstaller binaries for linux x86_64/arm64, macOS x86_64/arm64 and windows x86_64, plus openapi.json and one combined unsigned SHA256SUMS attached to the GitHub release (release-binaries.yml:64-88,160-171,256-278). (d) multi-arch GHCR images ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server in variants python, python-slim, python-minimal, java and golang (server.yml:318-418); the default image bakes ACP providers claude-code,codex,gemini-cli and capabilities vscode,browser,docker (server.yml:430,433; docker/Dockerfile:22,28), runs as non-root user openhands UID 10001 (Dockerfile:7-9,343), pins Node tarballs by SHA-256 (Dockerfile:209-216) and Debian by snapshot (Dockerfile:43). No cosign, sigstore, SBOM or provenance steps for PyPI, binaries or images (grep over .github found only the npm --provenance). Process: prepare-release.yml -> release PR (integration + examples labels) -> create-release.yml dispatches every publisher against the immutable tag (README-RELEASE.md:7-52). Release PRs get an approval-drift check and an OSV dependency diff (security-scan.yml:1-27,74-93). Policy: breaking SDK/REST changes need a deprecation runway of 5 minor releases (AGENTS.md:131-154).
code.tests_and_ci: pytest with asyncio auto mode, xdist, forked, timeout and cov (pyproject.toml:31-50,94-107); vitest for the TS client (clients/typescript/package.json:65-71). About 614 test_*.py files under tests/ (dirs sdk, tools, workspace, agent_server incl. stress/telemetry/docker_runtime/canvas_extensions, cross, examples, integration, fixtures; tests.yml:25-30), 28 LLM-backed integration scenario files (tests/integration/tests/{a,b,c,t}*.py), 31 vitest files (23 unit + 8 integration). 35 workflow files in .github/workflows. Main ones: tests.yml (per-package pytest gated by changed-files; Windows tools subset; live ACP/npm conformance only when ACP registry files change; stress suite; coverage run with --cov-fail-under=0, i.e. reported not enforced; lines 69-537); precommit.yml + .pre-commit-config.yaml (ruff, pycodestyle, pyright, yamlfmt, import-rule, tool-registration and dynamic-attribute gates; lines 3-63); server.yml (PyInstaller binary build and smoke test on ubuntu/macos/windows, OpenAPI check, 10-job multi-arch image build/push; lines 37-418); release-binaries.yml (5-runner binary matrix plus Docker manifest and /health smoke tests); agent-server-rest-api-breakage.yml (oasdiff, lines 31-37); persisted-settings-compat.yml; deprecation-check.yml; version-bump-guard.yml (SDK API breakage check, line 43); security-scan.yml; typescript-client-ci.yml (Node 22.12 and 24.x). Real-LLM runs (run-examples.yml, integration-runner.yml) go through the OpenHands proxy with repo secrets and are triggered only by labels or manual dispatch; default models are gpt-5.5, deepseek-v4-flash, minimax-m2.7, gemini-3.1-pro, claude-sonnet-4-6, with no GPT-6 entry (integration-runner.yml:6-12,57-58,117-132; run-examples.yml:68-80). tests/README.md:25 says integration tests run nightly, but integration-runner.yml has no schedule trigger.

risks: GPT-6.1 Sol is not a model id anywhere in the checkout (grep for 'gpt-6.1': no match). Nearest ids: gpt-6-sol (verified list, openhands-sdk/.../llm/utils/verified_models.py:14,115; routed to the Responses API by the 'gpt-6' substring, model_features.py:194-203) and gpt-5.6-sol (Codex-ACP picker, settings/acp_providers.py:376-382). The Codex-ACP curated list has only gpt-6-astra among GPT-6 ids, and ChatGPT-subscription login accepts only that list (llm/auth/openai.py:132-143,780-784), so gpt-6-sol would be rejected on that path. GPT-6 ids get no model-specific prompt variant (llm/utils/model_prompt_spec.py:37-51; context/prompts/sections/static.py:454-486) and no GPT-6 entry exists in the CI model table (.github/workflows/integration-runner.yml:117-132). Capability data comes from LiteLLM's model DB fetched from upstream main at import with no SDK override (tests/sdk/llm/test_model_features.py:3-6), and a LiteLLM supported_endpoints list overrides the SDK's substring fallback (model_features.py:344-359).

No dedicated deep-research harness in the repo (grep for 'deep research'/'citation': nothing relevant). The closest piece is the built-in web-researcher sub-agent: a markdown prompt plus the browser toolset, Tavily MCP (npx tavily-mcp@0.2.1, TAVILY_API_KEY) and mcp-server-fetch via uvx (openhands-tools/.../preset/subagents/web_researcher.md:1-19). Its 'include source URLs' and 'cross-reference at least 2 sources' rules are prompt text only (lines 62-88); no code verifies citations. It needs TaskToolSet, which is off by default, and built-in registration (preset/default.py:37-68,141-171); tests only assert registration (tests/tools/test_builtin_agents.py:95,107-111).

Isolation is opt-in and the default posture is permissive. Conversation(workspace=path) runs tools on the host (openhands-sdk/.../workspace/local.py:17-29; README.md:73); the default confirmation policy is NeverConfirm (conversation/state.py:123; conversation/request.py:131-135). The agent shell env strips only SESSION_API_KEY, OH_SECRET_KEY and OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_* (utils/command.py:25-30,57-67), so provider keys in the host env stay visible to agent commands. For ACP workers, request_permission auto-approves everything and default session modes are bypassPermissions / agent-full-access (agent/acp_agent.py:1602-1619; settings/acp_providers.py:514,550). The CLI subprocess gets the entire host os.environ plus the whole secret registry (acp_agent.py:2937-2951; conversation/secret_registry.py:262-264, where least-privilege scoping is marked deferred). One ACP step() is one complete remote turn (acp_agent.py:10-12), so an SDK per-step iteration cap does not appear to bound tool calls inside a turn (inference from the docstring).

Container hardening is uneven and the control plane is broad. DockerWorkspace runs `docker run` with no cap-drop, security-opt, memory/CPU or network-restriction flags and defaults to platform linux/amd64 (openhands-workspace/.../docker/workspace.py:104-106,235-252). The per-conversation Docker runtime (code-only, no README or doc found) adds --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, memory/CPU/pids limits and a loopback port, but keeps default networking and adds host.docker.internal (openhands-agent-server/.../docker_runtime/registry.py:409-434). The default image also bundles Docker Engine, gh and an OpenVSCode server (docker/Dockerfile:28,426,505,522). The server exposes bash, file and git endpoints (api.py:458-462) and is unauthenticated when no session key is configured (config.py:224-234; dependencies.py:36); loopback bind is the only default mitigation (__main__.py:282-294).

Supply-chain and release integrity. PyPI publishing uses a long-lived token with no OIDC or attestation (.github/workflows/pypi-release.yml:20-22,53,86); binaries ship with an unsigned SHA256SUMS (release-binaries.yml:256-278); image workflows have no signing or attestation step (server.yml:516-533); only the npm client uses --provenance (typescript-client-npm-publish.yml:68). ACP adapters are version-pinned but fetched from npm with `npx -y` at runtime unless baked in (settings/acp_install_catalog.py:78-98,101-116). load_public_skills=True (default False) clones github.com/OpenHands/extensions at ref main (sdk/skills/skill.py:1143-1146). CI model resolution clones another repo at run time (.github/run-eval/resolve_model_config.py:21-59). There is no SECURITY.md or disclosure policy in the checkout.

Telemetry and third-party surface (all off by default). `lmnr` is a hard dependency that activates on env keys (openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml:25; observability/laminar.py:244-260). posthog is already in the lock via browser-use (openhands-agent-server/pyproject.toml:24-26); the repo has no setting for browser-use's own telemetry, upstream default unverified. GraySwanAnalyzer sends conversation history to api.grayswan.ai when used (security/grayswan/analyzer.py:28-68). The ChatGPT-subscription path sends headers copied from the Codex CLI (originator codex_cli_rs) to chatgpt.com using a Codex public client id (llm/auth/openai.py:122-125,806-811); the SDK prints a consent banner citing OpenAI's consumer Terms of Use (openai.py:53-57).

Documentation and packaging drift. Agent-server README default host 0.0.0.0 vs loopback in code (README.md:42 vs __main__.py:282-285); Bearer header vs X-Session-API-Key (README.md:95 vs dependencies.py:19); storage layout (README.md:425-433 vs persistence_const.py:4-10); tests/README.md:25 'nightly' vs no schedule trigger (integration-runner.yml:6-12); the LLM.subscription_login docstring lists gpt-5.6/gpt-5.4/gpt-5.4-mini (llm/llm.py:3506-3513) though the accepted set is the Codex registry (openai.py:132-143,780-784); apptainer README names example 07 but the file is 08. openhands-agent-server declares aiosqlite, alembic, sqlalchemy and docker (pyproject.toml:8-10,16) that nothing in the repo imports. aiohttp and authlib are imported directly (llm/auth/openai.py:24-26) but declared in no dependency list (aiohttp only as a root constraint, pyproject.toml:11; authlib arrives via fastmcp, uv.lock:1059). The four package pyproject files have no license field and no LICENSE file sits in the package dirs (only repo-root LICENSE and clients/typescript/LICENSE). Root constraint-dependencies and exclude-newer (pyproject.toml:6-22) govern this repo's lock, while published metadata carries lower bounds (e.g. litellm>=1.93.0, openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml:18).

Resume, budget and maturity gaps. Without persistence_dir the SDK falls back to an in-memory store with a warning (conversation/state.py:509-519). The Conversation() factory defaults delete_on_close=True, including for RemoteConversation, whose close() sends DELETE for the server-side conversation (conversation.py:84,113,142,205; remote_conversation.py:1853-1863). ACP resume needs the persisted session id plus the CLI's own on-disk session store (agent/acp_agent.py:2989-3010). The cost cap max_budget_per_run exists only as a LocalConversation constructor argument and sub-agent frontmatter key, not in the Conversation() factory signature or the agent-server start request (local_conversation.py:237; conversation.py:122-149; conversation/request.py:93-160). The TypeScript client self-describes as alpha although versioned 1.50.1, and its pinned server contract is image 1.47.0 (clients/typescript/README.md:3-12; package.json:49-51). The critic is marked EXPERIMENTAL (agent/base.py:283-291). ACP integration shows churn: model lists are 'rollout/account-dependent' with dead entries removed, and agent-client-protocol is pinned <0.13 after a 0.11 break (settings/acp_providers.py:366-375; openhands-sdk/pyproject.toml:8).

checks.statement: PyPI packages (openhands-sdk, openhands-tools, openhands-workspace, openhands-agent-server). The README defers to an external Getting Started page that was not opened; command and package names come from an issue-template placeholder and the release workflow. Command: pip install openhands-sdk
checks.note: bug_template.yml:81 placeholder reads 'ex. pip install openhands-sdk, uv pip install openhands-sdk, pip install -e ., etc.'. pypi-release.yml:63-68 PACKAGES lists exactly the four names, each built with `uv build --package` (79-82) and published with `uv publish` (86). The four pyproject.toml files declare those names at version 1.50.1 (lines 2-3 each). README.md:80 does send installation to the external Getting Started guide. Caveat, not an error: openhands-sdk does not depend on openhands-tools (only tools, workspace and agent-server depend on sdk), so `pip install openhands-sdk` alone cannot run the README Quick Start, which imports openhands.tools.* (README.md:53-55).

LICENSE:1-21 is the standard MIT text ('MIT License', 'Copyright (c) 2026 OpenHands contributors'). README.md:10 badge alt text is 'MIT License'. The only other project license, clients/typescript/LICENSE:1 ('The MIT License (MIT)') plus package.json:87 "license": "MIT", agrees. The third LICENSE in the checkout is a test fixture. The four Python pyproject.toml files carry no license field, which matches the dossier's own risk note.

checks.statement: '--host default is 0.0.0.0' verified: no. Code defaults to 127.0.0.1 unless a session API key is configured, then 0.0.0.0; an explicit wildcard bind without a key only logs a warning.
checks.note: Agent-server README.md:30 and :42 say the default host is 0.0.0.0. __main__.py:215-222 sets default=None, with help text 'Defaults to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) when no session API key is configured'. Lines 282-285 resolve to '0.0.0.0' only when _auth_enabled() is true, otherwise to _LOOPBACK_HOST = '127.0.0.1' (:27). _auth_enabled() checks config.session_api_keys, from SESSION_API_KEY / OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0 or the config file (:30-48). Lines 286-294: an explicit wildcard host without a key only logs a warning. The dossier's 'no' verdict and its evidence are correct.
